narrative: Three years in, full-year 2021 net income set a new record at $48.3 billion, aided by a $1.8 billion fourth-quarter release of reserves built during the pandemic.

checks.a1: Supported again. 2021 net income reached a further record after the 2020 dip, consistent with the December 2018 quarter having been a blip rather than a lasting cycle turn.
checks.a2: Not supported yet. Rates were cut to near zero in 2020 and full-year net income fell as reserves were built. This one year does not settle how a future rate path affects income.
checks.a3: Unresolved. A strong capital ratio and ongoing branch and technology investment at the cutoff do not by themselves show how the bank would perform through a future downturn.
checks.a4: Not supported. The bank released reserves rather than building them in 2021, and net income set a fresh record. The earnings cycle has not yet shown a sustained top.
checks.a5: Choosing not to take a position is consistent with uncertainty. This outcome alone cannot tell us whether that was the better decision.

assumptions.text: The December quarter was market noise, not the credit cycle turning.
Higher rates will keep lifting net interest income.
Scale and capital will let the bank take share through the next downturn.
Rising provisions and expenses mark the top of the earnings cycle.
I don't have enough evidence to take a position either way.
